content: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners with production write access are a top attack path: a compromised runner gives direct access to whatever credentials/network paths it holds (in this case: IIS filesystem write + prod DB access). Runners are typically persistent (not ephemeral), so a compromised job can leave a backdoor for the next run. Best practices: default GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only, grant minimal per-job permissions, require approval for workflow runs from outside collaborators, monitor/log runner process activity, and treat the runner host as sensitive production infrastructure needing its own hardening/patching cadence.
